title: Maintainers' Handbook: Tokens & Visual Primitives Contribution + Deprecation Process
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose:
Create a single, practical Maintainers' Handbook that documents contribution rules, an executable review checklist, the RFC workflow, and the deprecation policy specifically tuned for tokens, buttons, tables, and charts. This is aimed at reducing bus factor for visual primitives and making changes predictable for product teams that depend on the system.

Scope (what this doc will cover):
- Contribution flow for design artifacts (tokens, Sketch/Figma tokens export, Storybook stories) and code (React components, CSS tokens, chart primitives).
- Approval matrix and required signoffs for types of changes (non-breaking token tweak vs breaking token rename vs API change in Button).
- A concrete review checklist (design + accessibility + engineering + infra + QA + product).
- RFC requirements and template examples for medium+ risk work.
- Deprecation policy and timeline with automated migration tooling recommendations (codemods, storybook deprecation banners, telemetry).
- Rollout gating and monitoring instructions (canary percentage, telemetry signals to watch).

Goals:
- Standardize what 'safe' maintenance looks like for tokens and visual primitives.
- Reduce surprises by forcing clear RFCs and measurable metrics for changes.
- Provide step-by-step instructions for maintainers to land, communicate, and deprecate features.

Out of scope: major redesign proposals that replace large swaths of primitives (these should be separate PRDs).

Deliverables:
- A single JSON/MD handbook file stored in Confluence + canonical README in the repo.
- A review checklist used as a PR template check.
- RFC template with examples for token migration and for chart API changes.
- Codemod starter scripts and a migration playbook.
review_checklist: Design QA: new token values documented in tokens.json and Figma token file; visual diffs in Storybook show intended change
Accessibility: color contrast (WCAG AA/AAA where applicable), focus order and keyboard behavior for interactive components
API Stability: for component props, document old and new behavior; provide default fallbacks for new props
Backward Compatibility: identify breaking changes and confirm migration helpers or opt-in flags
Automated Tests: unit tests for component behavior, snapshot and Chromatic visual tests for Storybook
Integration: smoke test in one product workspace using dedicated branch/deployment
Performance: charts: ensure <10% render time regression on typical datasets; measure memory footprint on large series
Observability: add telemetry events for new props/tokens if change affects runtime rendering or decision logic
Docs: update design tokens docs, migration guide, and changelog entry
Localization: confirm token changes do not affect layout for RTL or languages with longer strings
contribution_steps: 1. Open an RFC for any change that touches public token names, component prop surface, or chart data contracts (use RFC template below).
2. Create a working branch and update tokens.json / component files + Storybook stories; include before/after screenshots and a small demo app showing migration impact.
3. Run linting, style-dictionary build, unit tests and Chromatic visual tests locally; attach results to PR.
4. Request 2 design reviewers, 1 engineering reviewer (component owner), and 1 accessibility reviewer. Add labels: 'design-review', 'a11y', 'breaking-if-any'.
5. If the change is breaking, schedule a canary deployment and co-ordinate with product leads to enable feature flag for affected customers.
6. After approvals, merge and publish tokens package; create a changelog with migration steps and codemod if needed.
7. Monitor telemetry and error dashboards for 72 hours, then close the RFC with outcomes and lessons learned.
rfc_process: Thresholds that require an RFC: token renames, removal of public tokens, new chart data contract, changes to component SSR behavior, changes that are likely to cause visual regressions across products.

RFC template summary: problem statement; affected consumers (internal products + public SDKs); migration strategies; backward-compatibility matrix; rollout plan and monitoring metrics; risk/opportunity assessment; resource estimate.

Review cadence: RFCs are published as a PR in the design-system RFCs folder. All RFCs require 7 calendar days of review, then a final signoff from Design + Component Owner + Product (or an explicit exceptional approval).
Small changes (non-public tokens, minor spacing corrections) may use a lightweight RFC: 48-hour review and single owner approval.
Record decisions: RFCs get a short 'decision note' in the handbook and the RFC PR links to the final implementation PRs.
deprecation_policy_summary: When a token or component surface is to be removed or renamed, follow the 3-stage deprecation timeline: Announcement (T0): document change, add deprecated flag to tokens.json and show deprecation banner in Storybook; Grace period (T+90 days): codemods shipped, telemetry-enabled to track usage; Removal (T+180 days): remove token/component after cross-team migration and final review. For high-impact customers or enterprise Dedicated deployments, extend grace period to 6-12 months with direct outreach. All deprecations must include migration codemods where feasible and a fallback mapping in runtime for at least the Grace period.
migration_guidance: Provide codemod templates (jscodeshift) for token renames and prop name changes
Ship Storybook migration stories showing 'how to update' patterns
Create a 'migration-lab' branch in apps repo that demonstrates automated and manual migration paths
Include sample regex transforms for CSS token replacements and example Babel plugin snippets for runtime shims
owners_and_rotation: Primary maintainers: Design System team (rotation every 6 months)
Component owners: list in CODEOWNERS file; owner must provide PR review within 3 business days
Escalation: if owner unavailable, notify Design Leads and assign temporary owner from pool
rollout_and_monitoring: Canary plan: start at 5% of traffic for 24hrs, then 25% for 48hrs if no regressions, then 100%
Key telemetry to monitor: visual-regression-rate, a11y-issue-rate, client-errors-from-components, render-latency-by-component
Rollback criteria: >1% increase in client errors or >5% regression in visual-diff metric compared to baseline
Post-release: an automated smoke-runbook that runs critical stories and checks accessibility and snapshots
acceptance_criteria: Handbook published in Confluence and as README in design-system repo
PR template updated to include the review checklist items above
At least one RFC and one deprecation executed using this process as a pilot (documented lessons)
Codemod starter repo created with examples for token rename and Button prop rename
notes_and_decisions: 2026-03-11 — Decided: default deprecation timeline set to 180 days unless high-impact (extended).
2026-03-12 — Trade-off: require RFCs for public-token renames to avoid accidental breakage in consumer apps; this increases author overhead but reduces downstream incidents.
2026-03-13 — Agreed: integrate 'deprecation' flag into tokens.json and show it in Storybook with guidance and codemod links.
Decision: use style-dictionary for token builds and keep canonical tokens.json in the monorepo root.
